%=================================================================
% Abstract (<= ~200 words, one paragraph: background, methods, results, conclusion)
% All numbers: docs/publication/STAGE_C_MODES_RESULTS.md (2026-11-05).
\abstract{Authors state limitations, future work and open problems in their papers. Extracting these author-stated research gaps at scale could supply attributable inputs for automated idea generation. We present a three-stage funnel: rules discard text unlikely to contain gaps, a zero-shot natural-language-inference classifier flags candidate sentences without task-specific training, and a self-hosted large language model filters the candidates. The funnel returns source sentences, never generated text, and a single instruction sets the filter to high-precision, balanced or high-recall mode. On 40 randomized-trial reports with human limitation labels, high-precision mode raises precision from 29.1\% to 66.2\% at 84.9\% recall ($F_1$ 0.744); 40 held-out reports give $F_1$ 0.713. On future-work sentences from 209 NLP papers it reaches $F_1$ 0.760. On 34 test papers from a 230-paper arXiv and biomedical corpus labelled by an ensemble of language models, it reaches 86.6\% precision at 57.4\% recall across three gap types. On every dataset the modes trade precision for recall as intended, and the training-free classifier comes within 0.021 $F_1$ of a supervised PubMedBERT. The funnel sends 3.7--13 times fewer tokens than judging every sentence, but only 1.25--3.1 times fewer than one whole-paper call. We also find that letter case reveals the label in a public future-work dataset. Human validation and further baselines are in progress.}

% Keywords (3--10, semicolon-separated)
\keyword{research gap extraction; limitations; future work; scientific text mining; large language models; natural language inference; zero-shot classification; LLM filtering}
